name: Guatemala
summary_text: Guatemala demands real caution from trans visitors. Nothing criminalises being trans, but violence against LGBT people is severe and documented: Asociación Lambda's observatory recorded 147 cases of day-to-day violence and at least 29 murders of LGBTQIA+ people in 2022, with 35 victims saying they intended to flee the country. Guatemalan officials have explicitly excluded trans women from femicide-law protection on the grounds they are not “biological women.” There is no legal gender recognition and no SOGI hate-crime statute (a 2022 law actually increased penalties for “aggravated” LGBT visibility before being struck down). Congress has repeatedly advanced anti-LGBT initiatives (Law 5276, the 2022 “Life and Family Protection” law, later shelved after protests). The community is organised (Lambda, trans collectives) but under pressure. Tourist areas (Antigua, Atitlán) are accustomed to foreigners but not insulated from the general violence level.

sources.claim_summary: Wikipedia article on transfemicide (killing of trans women motivated by transphobic/misogynistic hatred): regional coverage includes North and South America; relevant background for Guatemala's context of violence against trans women.

sources.title: Human Rights Court Advances Gender Recognition in Latin America, But Challenges Remain - Arcus Foundation
sources.claim_summary: Arcus Foundation report (May 2024): the Inter-American Court's 2017 gender-identity opinion (Advisory Opinion OC-24/17) advanced legal gender recognition in El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Mexico, but a growing, vociferous opposition movement seeking to define gender in strictly binary terms is fomenting backlash in all four countries.

sources.title: Transgender rights bill introduced in Guatemala
sources.claim_summary: Washington Blade (Dec 2017): a transgender rights bill was introduced in Guatemala's Congress - the first legislative attempt at gender-identity protections in the country.

sources.title: Guatemala: Anti-Trans Bill Threatens Rights | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: HRW (Jan 2022): 'Guatemala: Anti-Trans Bill Threatens Rights' - documents legislative attacks on trans people, including bills that would erase gender identity protections and restrict legal recognition.

sources.title: First LGBT member of Guatemala Congress takes office
sources.claim_summary: Washington Blade (Jan 2016): the first openly LGBT member of Guatemala's Congress took office - a milestone for LGBT political representation.

sources.title: Latin America countries urged to abide by landmark LGBT rights ruling
sources.claim_summary: Washington Blade (Jan 2018): Latin American countries, including Guatemala, urged to abide by the landmark Inter-American Court of Human Rights ruling (Advisory Opinion OC-24/17) requiring marriage equality and gender recognition.
